description: Legal vendor and product market reference signals / calibration baselines (V1 scaffold). Every value ASSUMED until PAT has real cohorts.

baselines.sourceCrosswalk: Draws on ABA 2024 solo and 2 to 9 attorney bands, Clio 2024 solo and 2 to 4 lawyer spend bands, and Clio 2026 solo and small firm AI figures.
baselines.note: ASSUMED. Anchors: ABA 2024 solo AI use 18 percent, document assembly 37 percent, litigation support 27 percent, fee-based research 45 percent, 2FA 54.7 percent, CRM 31 to 39 percent; Clio 2024 software share of expenses 0.58 percent solo and 1.77 percent at 2 to 4 lawyers (blended to 1.2 percent); Clio 2026 solo AI use 71 percent counts any use and was not blended into expectedAiAdoption.

baselines.sourceCrosswalk: Draws on ABA 2024 2 to 9 and 10 to 49 attorney bands, Clio 2024 5 to 19 employee spend band, Clio 2025 smaller firms (20 or fewer employees) and Clio 2026 small firm AI figures.
baselines.note: ASSUMED. Anchors: ABA 2024 litigation support 38 percent at 2 to 9, AI use 30 percent at 10 to 49, budget exists 55 to 68 percent; Clio 2025 practice management use 71 percent at smaller firms; Clio 2024 software share 1.37 percent at 5 to 19 employees; Clio 2026 small firm AI use 75 percent (any use, not blended).

baselines.sourceCrosswalk: Draws on Clio 2025 mid-sized firms (21 or more employees), ABA 2024 10 to 49 attorney band, ABA 2023 50 to 99 lawyer band, ILTA 2026 under 50 lawyers band and MyCase 2025 51 or more lawyers band.
baselines.note: ASSUMED. Anchors: Clio 2025 mid-sized practice management use 38 percent against ABA 2023 case management 78 percent at 50 to 99 lawyers (blended to 0.65); Clio 2025 mid-sized technology spend about 2 percent of expenses; ABA 2023 conflict checking 89 percent at 50 to 99; ILTA 2026 GenAI use or exploring 85 percent under 50 lawyers; MyCase 2025 firm-wide GenAI 39 percent at 51 or more; ABA 2024 AI use 30 percent at 10 to 49.

baselines.sourceCrosswalk: Draws on ABA 2024 100 or more attorney band, ILTA 2025 and 2026 bands 50 to 149, 150 to 349 and 350 to 699 lawyers, and the Thomson Reuters Midsize peer group.
baselines.note: ASSUMED. Anchors: ABA 2024 litigation support 73 percent, fee-based research 78 percent, file encryption 76.3 percent, incident response plan 83 percent, metadata removal 84 percent, AI use 46 percent at 100 or more attorneys; ILTA 2025 laptop encryption 91 percent and cloud DMS 76 percent across all ILTA firms; ILTA 2026 GenAI use or exploring 94 percent overall. No survey publishes technology spend as a share of expenses for this band; Thomson Reuters 2026 reports growth (technology spend up 9.7 percent) only, so the share is null.

baselines.sourceCrosswalk: Draws on ILTA 2025 and 2026 700 or more lawyers band, the upper part of ABA 2024 100 or more attorney band, and the Thomson Reuters Am Law 100 and Second Hundred peer groups.
baselines.note: ASSUMED. Anchors: ILTA 2025 and 2026 GenAI use or exploring 100 percent at 700 or more lawyers; ILTA 2026 named AI product use Microsoft 365 Copilot 76 percent, CoCounsel 44 percent, Claude 44 percent, Harvey 43 percent across all ILTA firms; ILTA 2025 cloud first or mostly cloud 88 percent; Thomson Reuters 2026 technology spend up 9.7 percent and knowledge management spend up 10.5 percent (growth only, so share is null).
